description: Cross-binding conformance for esm-spec §4.2's RIGHT-HAND-SIDE structural `D` rule, in BOTH of its halves. RESOLVE: a `D` with `wrt: "t"` (or no `wrt`) denotes the total time derivative of its operand, and flattening rewrites it into the tendency the system already defines — a STATE gives its own `D(x)/dt ~ f`; an OBSERVED gives the CHAIN RULE, its defining right-hand side differentiated by the same rule one level down; a parameter or a literal gives 0; and `+ - neg * /` distribute by the sum, product and quotient rules. So `dxdt ~ D(x, t)` is `-k*x`, a model's scoped `D(Chem.A, t)` is the mass-action tendency §7.4 generated for the sibling reaction system, and `D(2*x, t)` over the observed `combo` is `2*(-k*x)`. REFUSE: a `D` the resolution CANNOT answer — an operand outside that closed set (`^`, a call, a reduction, a nested `D`), a name in no table, or a cyclic chain — is a rewrite-target reaching evaluation, and a conforming runtime MUST report `unlowered_operator` rather than invent a value for it, IN PARTICULAR NOT `0`. The two halves are gated together on purpose. Before this category all three Rust evaluators answered `D(anything) = 0` "for parity" with one another, so four shipped documents (`tests/end_to_end/land_atmosphere_hydrology.esm`, `tests/events/financial_climate_scenarios.esm`, `tests/valid/scoped_refs_nested.esm` and `tests/validation/mathematical_correctness.esm`) computed silent zeros and an inline test asserting a species tendency at t = 0 graded a configuration the model never ran; Python and Julia meanwhile refused BOTH halves with `unlowered_operator`, so the bindings disagreed in opposite directions on the same document. The refusal half is the one that can silently rot: `0` is a plausible-looking number, so `d_of_unsupported` and `d_of_cycle` each assert `expected: 0.0` — a binding that invents the value passes on the arithmetic and is caught only by the OUTCOME contract. VERDICTS and outcome CLASSES are compared, not a numeric golden: a refusal has no actual to record, and each binding's diagnostic text differs while the `unlowered_operator` code (esm-spec §9.6.3 constraint 6) is the cross-binding contract.

scope_excluded.go: No simulator and no inline-test runner, so this CATEGORY (which drives one) cannot be run here. NOTE that this is an exclusion from the category only, not from the rule: §4.2's resolution is a FLATTEN transform, and esm-libraries-spec §4.7.5 binds every library including the Core tier, so `pkg/earthsci-ast-go/pkg/esm/flatten.go` still owes it. It does not have it today — feeding `tendency_resolution.esm` through `Flatten` leaves all three right-hand-side `D` nodes standing where Julia, Python and Rust substitute them. Latent, because `tests/conformance/flatten/cases.json` carries no right-hand-side `D`. Tracked separately.
scope_excluded.typescript: No simulator and no inline-test runner, so this CATEGORY (which drives one) cannot be run here. Same caveat as Go: §4.2's resolution is a FLATTEN transform and `pkg/earthsci-ast-ts/src/flatten.ts` implements flattening, so it owes the transform even without a runner. It does not have it today — `flatten` leaves all three right-hand-side `D` nodes of `tendency_resolution.esm` standing. Latent, because the shared flatten corpus carries no right-hand-side `D`. Tracked separately.
scope_excluded.julia: TWO gaps in `run_inline_tests` — the runner every inline-test category drives — neither of them in the §4.2 transform itself. (1) It cannot READ a 0-D observed: `_evaluate_assertion`'s pointwise branch resolves the asserted name against the STATE VECTOR alone (`_scalar_slot`, src/inline_tests.jl:1253) with no state-free-observed fallback of the kind Rust's `scalar_observed` and Python's `_scalar_observed` provide, so every assertion here answers `scalar state '<name>' not found`. (2) It does not REFUSE an unresolvable right-hand-side `D`: the refusal fixtures build and solve without complaint and only fail at the assertion lookup, so the `unlowered_operator` contract is unmet on this path (the gate in `tree_walk/compile.jl` belongs to the OTHER runner). Julia DOES implement the resolve half in full, chain rule included — `flatten` step 3c — and that is pinned separately by `rhs_time_derivative_resolution_test.jl`, which asserts it through a STATE the runner can read (`l(3) = 31` requires the chained tendency to have resolved). A binding GAP, not a design decision: remove this entry once `run_inline_tests` can read a 0-D observed and refuses an unlowered `D`.

cases.note: Anchor: the ODE state itself, so a document that failed to build is distinguishable from one that resolved wrongly.
OWN-STATE form. D(x, t) = -kx*x = -3*2. The pre-fix Rust answer was exactly 0.
The tendency that the chained one names: d(b)/dt = 5 over [0, 3].
CHAINED form: d(l)/dt = sla*d(b)/dt = 10, so l(3) = 1 + 30. A binding that resolves only one level deep, or that zeroes the inner D, leaves l at its default 1.
SCOPED form: D(Chem.A, t) = -k*A = -0.5*4, a tendency that exists only because §7.4 generated it from the reaction list. This is the shape the reporter of issue #206 needed.

CHAIN RULE. combo is an observed, `combo ~ 2*x`, and it carries no d(combo)/dt equation — but its definition does, one level down: d/dt(2*x) = 2*(-k*x) = -12 at t = 0. Resolving it needs no differentiation rule beyond the product rule the resolution already applies, so refusing it would be an arbitrary stop one substitution short. The pre-fix bindings answered 0 (Rust) or refused (Python, Julia); both were wrong.

A parameter does not vary with t, so its derivative IS 0 and the resolution says so. This case used to be a refusal that asserted `expected: 0.0` precisely to catch a binding inventing that number — the guard has moved to `d_of_unsupported` and `d_of_cycle`, which assert the same 0 for shapes where 0 is genuinely not an answer. Kept as a `value` case because a binding that refuses a constant's derivative cannot express `D(alpha*u + beta*v, t)`, which is what `tests/validation/mathematical_correctness.esm` is about.

PRODUCT RULE over a compound operand: d/dt(scale*x) = scale*(-k*x) = -12, with d(scale)/dt = 0 because `scale` is a parameter. Same machinery as `d_of_observed` — the observed case reaches this one after substituting the definition — so the two must agree or the rule is not one rule.

The BOUNDARY of the closed set. `^` is evaluable-core arithmetic sitting immediately beside the operators the resolution does distribute (`+ - neg * /`), and differentiating it needs the power RULE rather than a substitution — so the resolution answers nothing and §4.2 requires a refusal. The intended value is -24 and the pre-fix answer was 0; the fixture asserts 0 so an inventing binding passes on the arithmetic and is caught only here.

A SELF-REFERENTIAL tendency: `D(x)/dt ~ k * D(x, t)`. Substituting would re-enter the same equation without end, so the chain guard stops and leaves the node standing. This case is what makes the guard load-bearing: a binding without one does not fail this fixture, it hangs or overflows its stack. The algebra would give 0 for k != 1, and the fixture asserts 0, so — again — only the outcome class separates a resolution from an invention.
